Marie Chen: Hi team — planning to move to Zurich in July for ~18 months. Quick Qs: does WFH stipend convert to CHF or stay USD? Do I need to enroll in Swiss health insurance immediately? Also curious about pension contributions and whether Redwood will put me on Swiss payroll or keep me on US payroll for the first pay period. Any checklist?

Liam (People Ops): Congrats Marie! TL;DR: stipend is still paid but we typically switch to local payroll when people become tax/residency liable. Health insurance in CH is mandatory from day 1 of residency, so you'll need local coverage. We'll run a payroll/benefits eligibility and propose timeline.

Marie Chen: Thanks — do we do COLA or stipend top-ups for high-cost locations like Zurich? And what about equity tax withholding if I stay on US payroll?

Omar (Payroll): Good Qs. For Zurich: we don't have an automatic COLA, but we sometimes approve a location premium on case-by-case for senior hires. Stipend: we can either keep USD transfers or convert to CHF; conversion affects tax reporting. If you remain on US payroll, equity tax withholding stays under US rules until you move to Swiss payroll. But Swiss authorities may tax options depending on residency date — Legal/Tax needs to confirm.

Sofia (Legal): Adding: Switzerland has specific social security (AHV) and occupational pension (BVG) rules. If you go on Swiss payroll, both employer and employee contributions apply. If you stay on US payroll but live in CH, we need to check whether a social security agreement applies and whether we must register a Swiss wage withholding. Also, multiple employees in CH would trigger entity/employer-registration review.

Liam (People Ops): Checklist (short):
- Submit Location Change in HiBob w/ move date + Swiss address
- Complete International Payroll Intake (payroll-bot link below)
- Upload proof of residence and copy of passport
- Benefits eligibility check: health plan, BVG enrollment if on Swiss payroll
- Expense/equipment: claim within 30 days of delivery in Expensify
- Stipend proration: pro-rated for move month

payroll-bot: International Payroll Intake: https://redwood.example/international-payroll-intake — please complete to open a payroll case.

Marie Chen: Helpful — timeline question: how long before my first Swiss payroll run should I expect the switch? I may have rent to cover.

Omar (Payroll): Typically 4-6 weeks from completed intake + docs to be set up on local payroll. We can do a one-off payment on US payroll to cover a partial month if needed. We'll flag any tax withholding differences.

Marie Chen: Perfect. One last: is mandatory Swiss health insurance eligible for Redwood benefits reimbursement?

Liam (People Ops): We usually don't cover mandatory local statutory premiums as part of our US healthcare plan. We can discuss a benefits allowance in some cases — will confirm after benefits eligibility check.

Marie Chen: Thanks all, I'll fill the intake and upload docs this afternoon.
